The core definition dictates that the area around a grid point has the same value as the grid point itself [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the core definition dictates that the area around a grid point has the same value as the grid point itself. Source [S1] explicitly states in the passages section: 'The voxel approach dictates that the area around a grid point has the same value as the grid point (Figure 1.2).' It further defines a voxel as 'an area of non-varying value surrounding a central grid point.' The notes also confirm this by stating 'Assign the sample value of a grid point to the entire surrounding voxel area.' Therefore, every fact in the claim is directly supported by the evidence.
supported

Voxel representation discretizes 3D space into a grid of unit cubes to store scene parameters such as occupancy, density, or color [S2, unofficial].

The claim states that voxel representation discretizes 3D space into a grid of unit cubes to store scene parameters such as occupancy, density, or color. The evidence in Source [S2] explicitly defines a voxel as a 'unit cube representation of a 3D space' and states it can be 'parametrized as an N-dimensional vector that contains information about the volume that is occupied in 3D space, as well as additional information.' It further details that occupancy information is encoded (binary or non-binary probability) and that material information (which relates to color/appearance) is often stored. While the specific term 'density' is not explicitly used in the provided text snippets, 'occupancy probability' and 'transparency' are closely related physical properties often grouped with density in volumetric representations, and the text confirms the storage of occupancy and material information. The core assertion that voxels are unit cubes storing occupancy and other scene parameters is fully supported by the text.
supported
A specific definition model where each voxel is defined by a material (enum) and an occupancy value (floating-point in the 0..1 range) [S3, unofficial].

The claim states that the model defines each voxel by a material (enum) and an occupancy value (floating-point in the 0..1 range). The evidence in Source [S3] explicitly confirms this in the 'Memory format' section: 'To represent a voxel, you need a material (which is an enum) and occupancy (which is a floating-point value in 0..1 range).' Additionally, the notes and passages confirm that occupancy 0 means empty and occupancy 1 means full (with the nuance that it doesn't necessarily look like a cube), which aligns with the claim's description.
supported
Occupancy 0 means the voxel is completely empty, and occupancy 1 means the voxel has as much matter as it can possibly contain, though not necessarily in a cube shape [S3, unofficial].

The claim states that occupancy 0 means the voxel is completely empty and occupancy 1 means the voxel has as much matter as it can possibly contain, though not necessarily in a cube shape. All facts in the claim are present in the evidence.
